name: N.R. Narayana Murthy
forbes_bio: N.R. Narayana Murthy is the legendary cofounder and retired chairman of Indian tech giant Infosys, in which he continues to hold a minority stake.
Murthy stepped down as chairman in 2011 after 30 years with the company but returned in 2013 to hand over management to a professional CEO in 2014.
In 2017, Murthy was in the news for raising concerns over alleged corporate governance lapses at Infosys, which the company denied.
The controversy led to the CEO's resignation and a board shakeup, which saw the return of retired cofounder Nandan Nilekani as nonexecutive chairman.
Murthy triggered a nationwide debate in 2023 when he suggested in a podcast that for India's productivity to improve, young Indians should work 70 hours a week.
forbes_facts: Murthy's son-in-law Rishi Sunak, a member of the Conservative party in the U.K and a former Chancellor, was Prime Minister until 2024.
His Harvard-educated son Rohan donated $5.2 million to Harvard University Press to set up the Murty Classical Library, a collection of ancient Indian texts.
His son Rohan has cofounded his own enterprise software firm called Soroco.
In March 2024, Murthy gifted Infosys shares worth nearly $30 million to his four-month-old grandson.

name: Ricardo Salinas Pliego
name_chinese: 里卡多·萨利纳斯·普利戈
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Ricardo Salinas Pliego runs Mexican TV broadcaster, TV Azteca, and retailer Grupo Elektra.
His Grupo Elektra targets lower middle class consumers who borrow money from his banking arm, Banco Azteca, to buy items at Elektra stores.
Elektra was founded in the 1950s by Ricardo's grandfather, Hugo Salinas Rocha.
In 2026, after a years-long dispute over tax claims and fraud allegations, Grupo Elektra agreed to pay nearly $1.9 billion to the Mexican government.
Currently, shares of Grupo Azteca are suspended from trading and Grupo Elektra is set to go private.

name: Zhang Hongchao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2024)
forbes_bio: Zhang Hongchao is the chairman of Mixue Group, the world's second biggest seller of freshly-made drinks by annual cups sold after Starbucks.
He started a shaved ice shop in 1997 in China with a homemade machine and opened the first Mixue Bingcheng store two years later.

Nearly all-franchised, the Mixue Bingcheng chain offers bubble tea, lemonade, coffee and other drinks as well as ice cream at dirt-cheap prices across more than 50,000 stores, including nearly 5,000 overseas.
The company went public in a $444 million Hong Kong IPO in March 2025.
His younger brother Zhang Hongfu, CEO of the company and also a billionaire, joined Mixue in 2007.

name: Frank Love
forbes_bio: Frank Love and his brother Greg are co-CEOs of Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, a truck stop and convenience store chains with over 600 locations in 42 states.
The $22 billion (est. sales) company was founded by his parents, Tom and Judy Love, in 1964.
Sister Jenny Love Meyer is chief culture officer and EVP; sister Laura has no role at the company.

name: Tatiana Casiraghi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2015-2019); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Billionaire heiress Tatiana Casiraghi joined Monaco's royal family in 2013 after marrying Andrea Casiraghi, fourth in line to the throne.
Tatiana and her brother Julio Mario Santo Domingo III inherited part of their grandfather's shares in SABMiller which is now part of Anheuser-Busch.
Tatiana co-founded Muzungu Sisters, an online retailer of artisan crafted goods from over 8 countries, with friend and fellow traveler Dana Alikhani.

name: Firoz Mistry
forbes_bio: Firoz Mistry is the son of the late Cyrus Mistry, the former chairman of Tata Sons, the holding company of the Tata conglomerate.
He inherited part of his family's 18.4% stake in Tata Sons after his father died in a car crash in 2022.
The chairman of the family's Shapoorji Pallonji group, a Mumbai construction giant, is his uncle Shapoor Mistry.
To reduce debt, the group raised $646 million by listing privately held construction and engineering firm Afcons Infrastructure in 2024.

name: Kei Hoi Pang
forbes_bio: Kei Hoi Pang founded and chairs Logan Property Holdings, a real estate developer headquartered in Guangdong province that targets the residential market.
The Keis' ownership in Logan in 2014 appeared to be controlled by daughter Perenna before clarifications by the company.
Logan went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2013.

name: Hussain Binghatti Aljbori
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Hussain Binghatti Aljbori is the founder and former chairman of Dubai-based luxury real estate developer Binghatti Properties.
He founded the company in 2008 and grew it into one of the largest property developers in the United Arab Emirates; he owns 100%.
Binghatti has launched branded luxury developments with automakers Mercedes-Benz and Bugatti and jeweler Jacob & Co.
Binghatti Properties raised $500 million in Islamic bonds, called sukuk, in 2024.
Binghatti's son Muhammad is now chairman of the company.

name: John Stanton
sec_insider_companies: MICROSOFT CORP (MSFT) - Director; COSTCO WHOLESALE CORP /NEW (COST) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: John Stanton is the chairman of the Seattle Mariners baseball team, serving as managing partner of a group of investors that has owned the franchise since 2016.
He made his fortune as an executive in the wireless telecommunications industry, helming four of the top wireless operators in the United States.
He formed Western Wireless Corporation in 1994; its spun-off subsidiary VoiceStream Wireless later became T-Mobile USA after a sale to Deutsche Telekom.
Stanton is currently a managing director of Bellevue, Washington-based venture capital firm Trilogy Equity Partners, which he founded in 2006.
forbes_facts: Other than during his time at university, Stanton has lived in the Seattle area for almost his whole life.

name: Jiang Yintai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Jiang Yintai chairs auto parts maker Shanghai Daimay Automotive Interior.
Daimay produces sun visors, seats and headrests, steering wheels and roof consoles.
Customers include GM, Ford, Chrysler, Volkswagen, PSA and Great Wall.
Jiang set up Daimay on the island of Daishan in the Chinese coastal city of Zhoushan in Zhejiang Province in 1982.
He moved the headquarters to Shanghai in 2002.

name: Clayton Zekelman
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Clayton Zekelman owns a stake in his family's steel business, Zekelman Industries.
The $3.3 billion (revenues) company is one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers.
The company has also pumped more than $1 billion into Z Modular, a division that is developing modular apartment complexes in places such as Texas, Arizona and Canada.
Clayton and his brothers, fellow billionaires Barry Zekelman and Alan Zekelman, split 100% ownership of Zekelman Industries.
They sold the company to the Carlyle Group in 2006 for some $1.2 billion, but bought the business back in 2011.
forbes_facts: One of Zekelman Industries' subsidiaries, Atlas Tube, produced steel for stretches of the Mexican border wall in Arizona.

name: Bruce Toll
forbes_bio: Bruce Toll cofounded homebuilding giant Toll Brothers in 1967 with his late brother, Bob (d. 2022).
Toll is the son of a multimillionaire investor who lost it all in the 1929 stock market crash and supported his family through the Depression by delivering laundry.
He and his brother built their first home in Chester County, Pennsylvania, then built Toll Brothers into one of America's leading luxury builders.
They took the $11 billion (fiscal 2025 sales) company public in 1986. It builds in more than 60 markets across the United States.
His BET Investments owns, manages, develops and leases mid-rise office buildings, office parks, retail complexes, apartment buildings and industrial space across the U.S.
